slides.title: Memory champions don't have special brains. They have a trick.
A roof falls in
slides.body: As Cicero tells it, the poet Simonides stepped out of a feast, the hall collapsed behind him, and he named the crushed guests by remembering where each had sat. A legend, but the method is real.

slides.title: Places keep things in order
slides.body: Pick a building you know and a route through it. Turn each thing you want to remember into a vivid image and leave one at each stop. To recall them, walk the route again.

slides.title: Inside the champions' heads
slides.body: A 2003 study scanned ten top memorizers. It found no exceptional intellect and no structural brain differences. Nine of the ten used this method.

slides.title: Six weeks: from 26 words to 62
slides.body: In a 2017 study, men new to memory tricks trained in the method for six weeks. Their average went from 26 words out of 72 to 62, and the gains held four months later.

slides.title: Then, a whole deck of cards
slides.body: Every card becomes a picture (the 7 of hearts is a rock, the king of spades a pirate) and every picture gets a room. The course ends with you memorizing a shuffled deck.
